newsitem.title: UK: USA Global Link cuts phone cost with Internet.
newsitem.headline: USA Global Link cuts phone cost with Internet.

text.p: International call-back operator USA Global Link Inc said on Wednesday it was poised to launch a global service that will slash the price of international phone calls by up to 90 percent by routing them through the Internet.
Called Global Internetwork, the 300-million-stg system does not require users to have computers and is the first global phone-to-phone Internet service.

In an attempt to shake up what it calls the "stifling control" and "smothering bureacracy" of giant telecoms companies, the system will be launched in 60 days in 10 countries including the U.S., Japan, the UK, France, Germany, South Africa, Hong Kong, Indonesia and Korea.

Bypassing costly charges of telecom companies at both ends of international calls, the technology also handles fax, data and video transmissions as well as voice. It can also operate computer-to-computer. "USA Global Link customers will be able to make a simple phone call to anyone, anywhere in the world, for a fraction of conventional international long-distance costs," the company said.
Calls will be instantly transformed from analogue into digital signal amd transmitted via the Internet computer network anywhere in the world, the company says.
It says the quality, a common problem with this type of call, will be equal to or better than current calls routed by satellite and far better than first-generation Internet telephony.
The U.S. company, which has said it is "ready to strike like lightning on technological advances", is announcing the new technology in London on Thursday.
